current_state: Energean's CEO floated a verbal concept (reported April 2022) to liquefy the company's Israeli-field gas via a floating LNG facility at Vasilikos, Cyprus for EU export. No FEED contract, site agreement, permit application, or FID has surfaced in any subsequent search through mid-2026.
missing_threshold_elements: No concrete step beyond a media remark: no site agreement, no FEED/engineering contract, no permit filing, no announced capacity/train count, no updated sponsor statement since 2022.
watch_for: Any FEED contract, site/land agreement, permit filing, or FID announcement specifically referencing Vasilikos FLNG; also watch whether Cyprus's actual 2026 gas-export plan (pipeline to Egypt for Aphrodite/Cronos) forecloses this concept entirely.
notes: Likelihood of revival looks low: Cyprus's May 2026 cabinet-approved Cronos development plan and the pre-existing Aphrodite plan both monetize via subsea pipeline to Egypt's existing LNG plants, not a new domestic liquefaction facility, reducing the strategic rationale for a competing Vasilikos FLNG concept.
